name: Oak Valley Forest
description: Temperate deciduous forest: four agents whose small losses are priced linearly (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1), the remaining forest degrading past the threshold along one placeholder curve, valued at a global temperate-forest mean per hectare. Illustrative: every parameter is a placeholder or low-confidence. Derivations: gaia/cases/definitions/CASE_NOTES.md.

units_per_ha.note: Chosen so the per-tree carbon gives ~200 t CO2/ha.

unit_value.note: Revenue per tree felled (one-off); no market source.

safe_threshold_ratio.note: Safe extraction threshold; under the area_loss damage model (Step 8d.1) the depletion beyond which the REMAINING resource starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs its average value.

annual_value_per_ha.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2012.07.005, Table 2 (read in full): temperate forest, total economic value Int$3,013/ha/yr minus climate regulation Int$152 = Int$2,861/ha/yr (2007 international dollars, 2007 price level; 58 estimates, Table 3); converted to EUR with the World Bank's PPP conversion factor for household final consumption (PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, the 'private consumption' series de Groot et al. used), Spain, 2007: 0.808165 EUR per international $ (World Development Indicators, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ESP/indicator/PA.NUS.PRVT.PP?date=2007&format=json, read 13 October 2026; gaia/currency.py)
annual_value_per_ha.note: Every agent; the dependency weights split it. Step 8g.6 (the owner's answer: convert international dollars to euros everywhere): 2,861 x 0.808165 = EUR 2,312.16/ha/yr in 2007 euros at Spanish purchasing power (it was used at face value as EUR 2,848, from figures partly typed from memory: 3,000 - 152; now read in Table 2). Not inflated to a later price year and no income adjustment (the owner's decision for benefit transfers, Step 8d.5). Climate regulation is left out because carbon is valued only by gaia.carbon (decision D3). A global temperate-forest mean, not a site valuation.

steepness.note: Degradation of the REMAINING resource past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1, as for Posidonia): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span, the same curve for every agent. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. Not fitted to field data (calibration regime B).

rate_schedule.source: Ramsey r = δ + ηg with δ 0.5%, η 1.35, g 1.3% (Drupp et al. 2018 expert survey, as cited in gaia.discount)

scarcity_rate.note: 2% relative price change of ecosystem services. Above the estimates of Drupp et al. (2024), 1.28%/yr for forests (CI 0.85-1.70) and 1.66%/yr aggregate (CI 1.40-1.92); kept until Step 8. Below the discount rate, so the PV converges.

horizon_years.note: A modelling choice; the outputs also report the PV at 50, 100 and 200 years (horizon sensitivity).

anchors.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2012.07.005, Table 2 (Int$/ha/yr, 2007 price level, read in full): temperate forest, water (provisioning) Int$ 191; Table 1: 32 of its 38 water estimates are market or cost-based values (direct market prices 5, factor income/production function 10, avoided cost 7, mitigation/restoration cost 1, replacement cost 9); converted to EUR with the World Bank's PPP conversion factor for household final consumption (PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, the 'private consumption' series de Groot et al. used), Spain, 2007: 0.808165 EUR per international $ (World Development Indicators, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ESP/indicator/PA.NUS.PRVT.PP?date=2007&format=json, read 13 October 2026; gaia/currency.py)
anchors.description: A market-based value (Step 8d.6): water (provisioning) Int$191/ha/yr x 40 ha x 0.808165 EUR/Int$ (PPP, Spain 2007), a global temperate forest mean, not a site valuation (verified in Step 8d.6; it was the case's anchor 'from memory')
